correctness.rationale: PASS. In a fixed undirected tree, an oriented reachability query equals conjunction of prescribed edge signs on its unique path. For a shattered set, all-one realizability forces orientation compatibility; one-negative/all-other-positive labeling forces a private edge of that query. Conversely, orient all positive paths consistently and reverse a distinct private edge of each negative query; other query paths cannot be affected, realizing every labeling. On a path, intervals each having private points form a strict two-sided antichain. A middle interval must contain a private point outside its predecessor and successor, forcing L_{i+2}>=R_i+2 and hence R_{i+2}>=R_i+d+1. Initial R1>=d,R2>=d+1 yield k<=2q+1_{r=d}; two overlapping length-d intervals per disjoint length-(d+1) block with last d-edge tail when r=d achieve equality. Independently brute-force maximized private-point interval systems for all 2<=d<=m<=8. This establishes the exact domain for all finite tree supports and for path m>=d>=1; finite brute force only corroborates.
